definitions.explanation: the physical act of cleaning and putting things in order after an activity

definitions.gloss: dealing with the aftermath; handling consequences
definitions.explanation: taking care of problems or complications that arise after an incident

examples.japanese: パーティーの{後始末|あとしまつ}をした。
examples.english: I cleaned up after the party.

examples.japanese: {自分|じぶん}の{後始末|あとしまつ}は{自分|じぶん}でしなさい。
{失敗|しっぱい}の{後始末|あとしまつ}に{追|お}われた。
examples.english: I was busy dealing with the aftermath of the failure.

examples.japanese: {食事|しょくじ}の{後始末|あとしまつ}は{私|わたし}がやります。
examples.english: I'll clean up after the meal.

examples.japanese: {不祥事|ふしょうじ}の{後始末|あとしまつ}で{大変|たいへん}だ。
examples.english: Dealing with the aftermath of the scandal is exhausting.

examples.japanese: {使|つか}った{道具|どうぐ}の{後始末|あとしまつ}を{忘|わす}れないでね。
examples.english: Don't forget to put away the tools you used.

notes:
{後始末|あとしまつ} refers to cleaning up or dealing with consequences after something happens.

COMPOSITION:
- {後|あと}: After, behind
- {始末|しまつ}: Disposal, dealing with

SENSE 1 VS SENSE 2:
- Sense 1: Physical cleanup (dishes, party mess, etc.)
- Sense 2: Figurative - handling problems, fixing mistakes

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {後始末|あとしまつ}をする (to clean up/deal with)
- {後始末|あとしまつ}に{追|お}われる (to be busy dealing with aftermath)
- {自分|じぶん}の{後始末|あとしまつ} (cleaning up after oneself)
- {失敗|しっぱい}の{後始末|あとしまつ} (dealing with the consequences of failure)

USAGE NOTES:
- Often implies responsibility for what happened
- "Clean up after yourself" is a common parental instruction
- Sense 2 often has a negative nuance (dealing with problems)

RELATED TERMS:
- {片付|かたづ}け (tidying up - more general)
- {尻拭|しりぬぐ}い (cleaning up someone else's mess - critical)
- {処理|しょり} (handling, processing - more formal)

REGISTER: Neutral. Common in everyday conversation.
